newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says it expects normal ties with Kuwait soon.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says it expects normal ties with Kuwait soon.

text.p: Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah said in remarks published on Monday that he expected full diplomatic ties with Kuwait to resume in the next few weeks after a rift caused by the 1990-1991 Gulf crisis.
"The coming few weeks will witness a full restoration of these ties," Tarawnah was quoted as saying in the daily Ad Dustour newspaper.

Kuwait has turned down several overtures by Jordan to normalise ties fully since the Arab Gulf state downgraded diplomatic ties and cut generous financial support to the kingdom and several other Arab states seen as sympathising with Baghdad during its 1990-1991 occupation.

In the latest move towards normalising ties, the two countries' state-owned airlines agreed on Sunday to resume direct flights between Amman and Kuwait for the first time since the 1990 Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
Tarawnah also said Jordan had successfully restored ties with most of the Arab Gulf states since relations s were ruptured after the Gulf crisis.
After distancing himself from Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein, Jordan's King Hussein has succeeded in improving ties with other Gulf Arab states including Saudi Arabia.

Jordan hopes to reopen its embassy in Kuwait,closed since the conflict, and send back its ambassador and wants Kuwait to elevate its downgraded diplomatic mission in Amman, run now by a charge d'affaires.
